### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **43** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **22** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface-signatures.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/root.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a7547c9f40e0dfab89a34f5e5b60f818af70d2`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **22** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface-signatures.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/root.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a7547c9f40e0dfab89a34f5e5b60f818af70d2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9275a54138667b9a6d539209b8b99008ab32b6d3` — the merge of head `388dcceb29f580b984200eceadfce9c723c33678` into base `05a7547c9f40e0dfab89a34f5e5b60f818af70d2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9275a54138667b9a6d539209b8b99008ab32b6d3 && git checkout 9275a54138667b9a6d539209b8b99008ab32b6d3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 05a7547c9f40e0dfab89a34f5e5b60f818af70d2 388dcceb29f580b984200eceadfce9c723c33678 && git checkout -B drift-repro 05a7547c9f40e0dfab89a34f5e5b60f818af70d2 && git merge --no-ff 388dcceb29f580b984200eceadfce9c723c33678

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a7547c9f40e0dfab89a34f5e5b60f818af70d2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 05a7547c9f40e0dfab89a34f5e5b60f818af70d2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `388dcceb29f580b984200eceadfce9c723c33678`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed read-only: card #19518 (body and all eight comments), the parent's design of record `5715762696` and rulings `5755653853` / `5904864936`, the split cards #20825 and #20827 (ruling `5910124148`), PR #20823's body and 75-file list, the net diff from merge-base `820d3f4f8e` to the head (+1432 / -132), and the head's check-runs. Scope tested is #19518 Scope 1-5 as amended by the seat: the "neither" refusal is #20827 and is not expected here.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes, each judged:

1. **New kind `picklist`** — `MetadataTypeSchema` member, `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` row (`loadOrder` 8, below `object` at 10 and `field` at 20; `allowRuntimeCreate: false`, `allowOrgOverride: false`, `supportsOverlay: false`; `filePatterns` `**/*.picklist.ts|yml|json`; `domain: 'data'`), `BUILTIN_METADATA_TYPE_SCHEMAS` binding, `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` and the regenerated meta-url map, `check-liveness` `GOVERNED`. **Right.** Matches Scope 1 and the `capability` precedent for a package-owned kind (ADR-0088 clause 2 is met by the file loader, which is registry-derived). Two consequences that are live on `main` the day this lands: `GET /meta/picklist` and `/meta/picklists` list (empty until #19519 registers items) instead of refusing an unknown type, and `PUT /meta/picklist/NAME` is refused 403 `not_creatable` on every kernel because the derived `CODE_ONLY_TYPES` set now holds `picklist` (both pinned in `metadata-protocol`). The registry comment claiming that refusal is true at land time.
2. **`PicklistSchema`** `{ name, label, description?, options }` — `strictObject`, `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` for `name` (the `mapping` precedent), ADR-0010 envelope spread, aliases `values|choices|items` to `options` and `title|displayName` to `label`, `definePicklist` on the root barrel. **Right.** `options.min(1)` is one step past the ruled shape (`SelectOption[]`) and is correct: an empty shared list is the ADR-0078 dead choice at list level, and the message says so. `SelectOptionSchema` is reused verbatim — no second option shape, as ruled.
3. **`PicklistExtensionSchema`** `{ extend, options min 1 }`, `strictObject`, `guidance` on `remove` and `label` as wrong-layer pointers, aliases `picklist|target|name|extends` to `extend`; stack collections `picklists` and `picklistExtensions`, both `concat` on compose. **Right** — additive only per design item 4; no key can remove or rename, and the guidance says where such a change belongs.
4. **`FieldSchema.picklist`** (`SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema`, optional) with a superRefine that refuses it on a non-option type at path `picklist` and refuses `picklist` + `options` at path `options` with the prescription; the old `picklist` to `options` alias removed; `valueSet|globalValueSet|optionSet` now alias to `picklist`. **Right.** Pure widening: before this PR every `picklist` key on a field was an unknown-key refusal, so nothing accepted on `main` is refused now. The option-type set in the message (select, radio, multiselect, checkboxes, tags) equals `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` plus `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES`. "Neither" is deliberately not refused (seat ruling; #20827, ruled A after this PR).
5. **`Field.select` overloads** — the new `selectFromPicklist` form returns `{ type: 'select', picklist, ...config }` with no `options`; a call handed both keeps both and reaches the door refusal (pinned). **Right.** One unstated widening rides with it: the inline form's parameter type moved from `SelectOption[] | string[]` to an array of `SelectOption` or `string`, so a mixed array now type-checks (the runtime already mapped elements one by one; the graduation of `field.test.ts`'s two TS2322 debt entries is the measurement). Public type surface, not mentioned in the changeset, and `Field` carries no hash in `api-surface-signatures.json` so no baseline moved. Right in substance (the type now matches the runtime); `minor` covers it.
6. **`PicklistServedFieldSchema`** — `looseObject { picklist, options min 1 }`, the Scope 3 shape. **Right**, and the strictness ledger row classifies it as a served passthrough by design. It is a declared contract with no producer on `main` at land time (see item 7 and the text judgments below).
7. **`checkFieldCompleteness`** counts a `picklist` string as the field's option source; the `fix` names both keys. **Right after #19519 lands; an interim at land time that the record must name.** On `main` today nothing resolves the reference, so a `{ type: 'select', picklist: 'x' }` field now parses, passes the ADR-0078 completeness gate (which used to be an error for a select with nothing to choose), and is served with no options and no server-side value check — the exact case the rule names. The compensating control is real: `field.picklist` is ledgered `planned` with `authorWarn` and an `authorHint` that says keep inline `options` on fields that must work today, and the `lintLivenessProperties` authoring rule is `advisory`, `commands: ALL` (`os validate`, `os build`, `os lint`), severity warning, never fatal. Studio cannot author the key (the metadata-form reconciliation omits it). This is the ruled spec-first sequencing (`5755653853`, `5904864936`) and the seat accepted it in `5908214854`; judged right as the interim, with the moment named.
8. **Translation face** — `picklists.NAME.{ label?, options }` on `TranslationDataSchema`, `PlatformTranslationDataSchema` and `TranslationItemSchema` (strict entry, aliases, `picklist` to `picklists` alias on all three doors), the ten-to-eleven group prose updated in six places, `translatePicklist` registered so `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES` gains `picklist`, and `translateObject` letting a picklist-bound field inherit `picklists.NAME.options.VALUE` with a field-level entry winning. **Right.** The "field-level wins" precedence is one step past Scope 4's wording ("field-level remains for inline options") and is within the design: the more specific entry wins, and the seat accepted it by name. Note the extractor never scaffolds a field-level option key for a picklist-bound field (pinned), while the resolver honours a hand-written one — consistent, not a gap.
9. **`os i18n extract` walk** (`walkPicklists`) — `picklists.NAME.label` via `pushEntry`, `picklists.NAME.options.VALUE` with the #8543 derived rule, an extension's options keyed under the list it extends, new `picklist` coverage source so `os lint` reports `i18n/missing-picklist` (`lint.ts` forms the id from the source), fixture member `parity_tier`, six-test pin. **Right**; the walk skips an option whose `value` is not a string, and `SelectOptionSchema.value` is a string, so nothing is lost.
10. **`driver-sql`** `FIELD_KEY_STORAGE_CLASS.picklist: 'presentation'`. **Right** — the option code lives in the select's own column; the reference is metadata.
11. **Census** — every enumerating pin moved (type-schema closure 25/26 to 26/27, create-seeds `KNOWN_UNSEEDED`, form-reconciliation omit row, lint `authorWarnedProperties('field')`, metadata-protocol `CODE_ONLY_TYPES` with a probe and the field property count 74 to 75, recovery-doors bootstrap set, platform-objects 27 to 28 types / 10 to 11 bare / 16 to 18 leaves / 657 to 658, runtime parity cells, CLI `GATED_AT`, showcase `KIND_COVERAGE` and `STACK_COLLECTION_COVERAGE` waived to #19519, `check-stack-collection-maps` waiver rows written as PENDING rows that fail stale when #19519 lands, liveness README 40 to 41 governed types plus shards, strictness ledger 158 to 161 sites, llms.txt, doc counts 27 to 28 / 29 to 30 / 1521 to 1524, generated baselines). **Right**; the green check-runs on the head are the proof for every pinned one. Two unpinned enumerations of registered kinds did not move: `packages/metadata/src/serializers/typescript-serializer.ts` `ANNOTATION_BY_METADATA_TYPE` (named in neither report; no picklist item can reach it before #19519 registers one) and `packages/metadata-core/src/types.ts` `MetadataTypeSchema` (named by the dev; its "lockstep" comment was already false in both directions before this PR, no pin). Both belong to the runtime layer; see ③.

Author-shown and AI-facing text, each sentence tested against the tree:

- `FieldSchema.picklist` describe (copied by generation into `field.mdx`, `object.mdx`, `migration.mdx` and the JSON schema): "The server resolves the reference: the field clients read carries the resolved `options`." **Over-broad at land time.** On `main` when this PR lands nothing resolves the reference and a picklist-bound field is served without options — the changeset says exactly that one sentence later, and `field.json`'s `authorHint` says it to the author at lint time. True only after #19519 lands. The same present tense sits in the `picklist` docblock in `field.zod.ts`, in the `PicklistServedFieldSchema` docblock ("Every consumer that reads `field.options` today … nothing a client does changes"), and in the pair-refusal message ("the shared list supplies them"). `picklist.mdx`'s own prose is conditional ("once the reference is resolved") and is fine. - `field.zod.ts` comment and the `picklist.test.ts` pin that "neither on a select/radio is the completeness gate's error, not a parse refusal" — **true now**; ruling `5910124148` (A) moves that refusal to the door after this PR lands, at which point this comment and pin move with it. Stated so the next author does not read it as permanent.
- `PICKLIST_HISTORY` ("Until this shape was closed these would have been dropped silently …") — a counterfactual, phrased as one; the kind was born closed. Acceptable.
- `.changeset/19518-picklist-kind.md` — every bullet holds: the kind and its registry facts, the reference and its two refusals, the completeness predicate, the served shape with the explicit "This release does not resolve the reference", additive extensions, the translation face with field-level precedence, the Studio type label in four bundles, the extraction walk and `i18n/missing-picklist`, the SQL classification. The one sentence that is true only after another PR is the `picklist` describe quoted above, and the changeset's next sentence names that moment itself.
- PR body, including 维护者速读 — every reading verified on the tree: `SKILL.md` 489 lines before and after; bytes 23313 to 23306; tokens (ceil bytes/4) 5829 to 5827 against the 5833 ceiling in `check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`; skills package `SKILL.md` lines 4396 unchanged; 1 of 75 paths governed (`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`, Tier H); 1564 changed lines; the hunks at lines 43-45 and 453; `4049ae31ba` touches only that file (+5/-5); `595621d35c` is the split that moved Part 3 to `references/operations.md`. "Every pin that enumerates registered kinds or `FieldSchema` keys moves with the kind" is true of pins; the two unpinned enumerations are named in ③. "Part of #19518", #20827 ruled A after this PR, #20825 for the CLI path — all match the rulings.
- **`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` hunk, read as text an AI author acts on.** The addition lists `picklists` and `picklistExtensions` after `objectExtensions` among the `defineStack()` top-level keys — required by `check:skill-top-level-keys`, and true: both keys parse. An author who writes them today gets a stack that loads and a field-level advisory warning telling them the reference is not resolved yet; the skill page itself carries no such note, and the ledger is the mechanism that does. Cut 1 ("covered in **Part 3 — Operations** below" to "in [Part 3 — Operations](…)"): the stated reason holds — on the base tree the only Part 3 text below line 452 is the moved-verbatim pointer at line 479; the content is in `references/operations.md` since `595621d35c`; the link target is unchanged, so an author following it lands where they did before. Cut 2 ("High-level cheat sheet" to "Cheat sheet"): redundant, as stated; the block's content is untouched. Nothing an author needs left the page.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec`: **`minor`** — matches the diff. New published kind, new `FieldSchema` key, two new stack collections, a new translation group on three doors, new exports (`PicklistSchema`, `PicklistExtensionSchema`, `PicklistServedFieldSchema`, `definePicklist`, the `Picklist*` types, `translatePicklist`, `PicklistLike`) all recorded in the api-surface, export-origins and declaration-map baselines. Widening only; nothing an author could write on `main` is refused now (the alias removal changes a refusal's suggestion, not the accept set).
- `Clause-②: yes` on the claim and the PR body; `yes (widening)` on the changeset, which is where AGENTS.md says the arm is read. Consistent with a new kind and a new `Field.select` reference; `yes` takes at least `minor`, satisfied. Correct.

A stricter reading would call the new rule id `i18n/missing-picklist` new functionality and say `minor`; either level leaves the release the same, since spec's `minor` lifts the workspace. Not a blocker.

## 维护者速读 · 2026-09-30T13:51Z

`domain:spec` seat 5(`session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1`)。这是终稿，由本席对照 diff 写成。本 PR 受管的部分只有一个文件:`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`。审核记录是达档复核 PASS `5912646092`。

**改了什么**
- 本 PR 新增共享选项集 `picklist` 这一元数据类型。技能文档的顶层键清单(第 43 行起)因此加上 `picklists`、`picklistExtensions` 两个键。
- 同一文件 CLI 小节的一句指路文字(第 453 行附近)删了两个词：已失真的「below」(Part 3 已由 `595621d35c` 拆到 `references/operations.md`)和与 cheat sheet 重复的「High-level」。
- 读数：文件 489 行不变;token 从 5829 降到 5827,上限 5833;技能包总行数 4396 不变。

**为什么改**
必需门禁 `check:skill-top-level-keys` 要求技能页的清单与 schema 一致。页面上没列的键,AI 作者就不会写。

**风险与代价(含回滚)**
- 只改文字，链接目标不变，作者需要的内容一处都没删。
- 回滚办法是 revert `4049ae31ba`;但如果不同时去掉这两个 stack 键，该门禁会重新变红。
- 另外，本 PR 还要补一轮只删文字的修改：`FieldSchema.picklist` 的说明里「服务器会解析引用」一句，要等运行时卡 #19519 落地才成立，先删掉。这一轮不碰技能文档。

**席位意见**
